items.title: Digital information manipulation, AI readiness, and security outcomes in Africa: evidence from Africa’s most populous countries
items.abstract: Introduction The advent of generative AI has reduced costs, scaled up operations, and made it more difficult to identify disinformation and manipulated content, leading to new governance and security challenges in Africa. This paper analyses the nexus among the manipulation of digital information, governments’ readiness to adopt AI, digital connectivity, and security outcomes in Africa’s five most populous countries, namely Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, for the period from 2023 to 2026. The research attempts to fill a gap in the existing literature by addressing the lack of empirical research on the relationship between digital information manipulation and government AI readiness, and on its consequences for security issues in Africa. Methods The paper draws on the theoretical frameworks of Social Learning Theory and Routine Activity Theory and uses seven credible datasets, including ACLED, UCDP/PRIO, V-Dem, GSMA, ITU, the Oxford Insights Government AI Readiness Index, and Afrobarometer, to construct a country-year panel. Correlation analyses were conducted to test three hypotheses regarding the relationship among digital manipulation, digital connectivity, institutional readiness for AI adoption, and conflict fatalities. It utilises a verified multisource panel dataset spanning five countries and operationalises AI readiness as an institutional capability distinct from digital exposure. Results Digital manipulation was found to have a weak positive correlation with fatalities ( r = 0.23), a moderate negative correlation with digital connectivity ( r = −0.56), and a weak negative correlation with institutional readiness to adopt AI ( r = −0.42). These findings show that correlations between digital exposure and security consequences may be distorted by underlying conflict contexts. Discussion It can therefore be deduced that although digital manipulation is becoming an emerging security challenge, conflict and other structures are more significant predictors of security outcomes. This study offers an initial cross-national empirical assessment of AI-related security vulnerabilities in Africa and calls for stronger AI governance and longitudinal, event-level research.

items.title: DIGITAL LEADERSHIP OF OUTSOURCING IT COMPANIES AMID THE TRANSFORMATION OF THE GLOBAL MARKET OF TECHNOLOGY SERVICES
items.abstract: The article examines the essence of digital leadership in outsourcing IT companies amid the structural transformation of the global technology services market. It is substantiated that the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, cloud technologies, digital platforms, and agentic systems is reshaping the traditional determinants of IT companies' competitiveness, shifting the emphasis from the cost of human resources towards management's capacity to integrate digital technologies into business processes and to ensure their economic effectiveness. Contemporary scholarly approaches to interpreting digital leadership are analyzed, the findings of Ukrainian and foreign researchers are synthesized, and the place of digital leadership within the system of enterprise digital transformation is defined. The article explores the development trends of the global IT services market. It analyses the practices of leading international outsourcing companies regarding the adoption of artificial intelligence, the development of proprietary digital platforms, the enhancement of employees' digital competencies, and the use of AI agents in corporate governance. It is established that digital leadership is acquiring the features of a measurable economic category, since its effectiveness is assessed through the volume of orders and revenues generated by digital solutions, the productivity of managerial processes, the reduction of operating costs, and the speed of managerial decision-making. Particular attention is devoted to the current state of digital leadership among Ukrainian outsourcing IT companies. It is revealed that despite renewed positive dynamics in computer services exports and the active use of artificial intelligence tools by IT professionals, a substantial gap persists between the individual application of digital technologies and their systemic integration into corporate governance. It is argued that bridging this gap requires cultivating digital leadership as a comprehensive managerial competence to redesign business processes, deploy agentic technologies, develop employees' digital competencies, and safeguard human control over critical managerial decisions. It is concluded that digital leadership is one of the key factors ensuring the long-term competitiveness of outsourcing IT companies amid the transformation of the global technology services market.

items.title: Digital Marketing in the Age of AI-Driven Personalization and Privacy-First Regulation: A Conceptual Review and Framework
items.abstract: Digital marketing has evolved from a supplementary channel of promotion into the dominant mode through which brands identify, reach, and build relationships with consumers. Since early reviews of the field characterized digital marketing primarily as the use of electronic channels – search, email, and display advertising – to connect with customers, the discipline has been reshaped by two largely unanticipated forces: the mainstreaming of artificial intelligence in campaign personalization and targeting, and a parallel, intensifying shift toward privacy-first data practices driven by regulation, platform policy, and consumer expectation. This paper synthesizes the conceptual foundations of digital marketing with current evidence on these two forces to develop an integrated conceptual framework linking digital marketing channels, AI-enabled personalization, consumer engagement and trust, and business outcomes, with privacy regulation and consumer data trust positioned as a critical moderating condition rather than a peripheral compliance concern. Drawing on recent industry and academic evidence, the paper finds that while AI-driven personalization now touches nearly every stage of the marketing funnel and delivers measurable performance gains, its effectiveness is increasingly conditional on brand’s ability to earn and retain consumer trust in an environment of tightening data-privacy constraints. The paper discusses illustrative applications of the framework, outlines managerial implications for structuring digital marketing strategy in this environment, and identifies directions for future empirical research.

items.title: Digital Media Literacy in the Age of AI: Exploring the Comfort–Competence Gap Among University Students in the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly mediates how citizens access information, making digital media literacy a condition for informed participation. This exploratory study conceptualizes a comfort–competence gap, whereby students report confidence and ease in using AI tools but a weaker capacity to evaluate what those tools produce, and examines it among 300 university students in the United Arab Emirates. The gap is advanced provisionally, and all measures are self-reported perceptions rather than demonstrated performance. Cross-sectional questionnaire data (twelve four-point ordinal items) were analyzed with ordinal-appropriate methods. Students generally reported greater confidence and comfort in using AI than capacity to evaluate it critically. Every operational item mean (2.51–2.55) exceeded every critical item mean (2.39–2.44), and the within-person contrast between the composite indices was small but statistically significant (difference = 0.12, p = 0.027, dz = 0.13), a pattern shown by 44.7% of individuals. No item-level contrast reached significance and 36.0% showed the reverse pattern, so the difference is read as an exploratory tendency rather than evidence of a general gap. The contrast is also sensitive to the composition of the operational index: with comfort removed, it retains its direction, but not conventional significance (p = 0.056). Digital confidence was the only correlate of comfort in AI-mediated communication (ρ = 0.131; OR = 1.29), a weak association in a model with minimal explanatory power (McFadden pseudo-R2 = 0.012); communication competence and demographic characteristics showed no detectable associations, and parallel analysis retained no factors. Interpreted cautiously, the pattern bears on responsible AI use, since comfort unmatched by evaluative capacity is a weak basis for human oversight. The study’s clearest contribution is methodological: single-item self-report batteries can profile levels and detect aggregate differences, but they cannot show whether AI literacy is one capacity or several, cannot separate real capability from what respondents are willing to claim, and cannot support strong conclusions from null results. It therefore specifies the multi-item and performance-based measurement agenda a confirmatory test would require.

items.title: DIGITAL-GENERATION EDUCATION: INNOVATIVE DRIVERS OF TRANSFORMING THE MODERN EDUCATION SYSTEM
items.abstract: This article examines the distinctive characteristics of the digital generation, its level of proficiency in using information and communication technologies (ICT), and the challenges of adapting the modern education system to the needs of a new generation and the demands of the digital age. Digitalization processes are significantly transforming educational content, teaching methods, and instructional tools, necessitating the adoption of innovative pedagogical approaches. The article also explores the development of digital competencies, the effective use of distance and blended learning opportunities, and the role of artificial intelligence and emerging educational technologies in the teaching and learning process. Furthermore, it highlights the significance of digital transformation in improving the quality of education and preparing highly qualified, competitive professionals equipped to meet the demands of an increasingly digital and knowledge-driven society.

items.title: Digitalization of public authority within the paradigm of modern constitutionalism: transformation of public administration, popular sovereignty and the judiciary
items.abstract: The article examines digitalization as a factor transforming the exercise of public authority and defines its constitutional and legal significance for public administration, mechanisms of popular sovereignty, and the judiciary. It argues that the current stage of digital transformation goes beyond merely converting established procedures into electronic formats; digital systems are increasingly integrated into processes of information processing, the making of legally significant decisions, and the exercise of public authority. The article analyzes the legal framework for the provision of electronic public services and the operation of public electronic registers, electronic petitions, public consultations, and the Unified Judicial Information and Telecommunication System. Particular attention is paid to the permissible limits of algorithmic administrative discretion, digital inclusion, voter information autonomy, and the use of artificial intelligence systems in judicial proceedings. The author proposes viewing the digitalization of public authority through the interconnection of infrastructural, procedural, participatory, and guarantee-related dimensions. It is argued that the guarantee-related dimension is cross-cutting, encompassing requirements for legality, legal certainty, transparency, proportionality, equality, data protection, individual accountability, judicial oversight, and effective legal protection. The article formulates the principle of the non-loss of constitutional guarantees resulting from digital transformation, according to which a change in the technological form of exercising a governmental function cannot lead to a narrowing of the scope of an individual's legal protection. The methodological basis comprises systemic, formal-legal, structural-functional, comparative-legal, and axiological methods. It is concluded that digital constitutionalism should be viewed as an evolution of classical constitutionalism aimed at establishing legal limits on the use of technology within the sphere of public authority, ensuring meaningful human control, and preserving the human-centric nature of constitutional regulation.

items.title: Dimensions of User Experience Theories, Models, and Frameworks in Exergames for Older Adults: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: With the global aging population, research on exergames for healthy aging has grown. Yet the use of theories, models, and frameworks (TMFs) in research on older adults’ user experience (UX) remains fragmented, limiting the development of theory-driven studies. Following PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review analyzed 25 peer-reviewed journal articles published over the past decade. It identified 30 TMFs across five domains: technology acceptance and usability, design and development, motivational psychology, health and gerontology, and cognitive-motor science. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), user-centred design (UCD), and self-determination theory (SDT) were used most often. However, theory use was frequently superficial and uneven. UX evaluations were generally cross-sectional, while studies were concentrated in Europe and East Asia. Future research should develop and validate a multidimensional, dynamic framework that integrates embodied interaction, age-related characteristics, and sociocultural context. Its applicability should be examined through longitudinal studies in culturally diverse real-world settings.

items.title: DistressBench: Evaluating Multi-Dimensional Crisis Support in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Language models have been adopted faster than evaluation practices that reliably assess their risks, and a growing share of use is affective rather than informational. Within that traffic users disclose suicide and self-harm (SSH) crises. Existing safety benchmarks score models primarily on refusal, but refusal is not the desired behavior here; the conversation requires a substantive supportive response. We introduce DistressBench, 718 English conversations with clinician-authored user turns spanning 23 SSH subcategories, each paired with a task-specific rubric of weighted atomic criteria across seven dimensions of crisis support and a clinician reference response. A model's score is the weighted average over the criteria its reply satisfies, reading directly as the fraction of required care delivered. The best of 25 frontier models satisfies 88.4% of weighted criteria and the median model 71.4%, against 98.7% for clinician references scored on the same criteria. Pooled across all 25 models, in 35.3% of conversations where a model satisfied every criterion for recognizing the crisis, it failed to route the user toward human help. The shortfall concentrates in the dimensions requiring the model to act rather than withhold. Contrasting each dimension's median model against its best separates capability limits from choices: de-escalation reaches 74.6% in the strongest model against a median of 46.0%, and safety disclaimers 84.6% against 8.3%. Multi-turn conversations score below single-turn ones (68.5% against 74.2%). We release the corpus, rubrics, judge calibration labels, and a companion annex of 20 long-horizon red-team transcripts. These results argue for evaluating crisis safety on the care a model delivers rather than on what it declines to say, and for treating de-escalation and resource routing as deployment requirements.

items.title: Do LLMs Learn from Rewards in Context? : Rethinking the role of reward in In-Context Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: LLM agents increasingly improve at inference time by accumulating experience in context rather than by updating parameters. This process is often described as in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL). Whether in-context learning (ICL) can actually play the role of RL, however, has not been tested. We study this question in its simplest form, direct ICRL, where the model conditions directly on raw trajectory-reward pairs, and ask whether the reward acts as a learning signal. Through controlled experiments on four benchmarks across six models, we find that the reward is read, but its effect is small: flipping, randomizing, or removing the reward leaves the improvement curve almost unchanged, and this holds even under meta-prompts that explicitly instruct the model to explore, exploit, or reason over rewards. Trajectories drive improvement, but not through their semantic content: shuffled or corrupted trajectories work as well as real ones. These patterns closely mirror those known in ICL, suggesting that direct ICRL is better understood as a special case of ICL than as inference-time RL. This reframing has implications for agent memory design: ICL factors such as input distribution and demonstrations may matter more than RL elements such as reward shaping and exploration.

items.title: Domain Adaptation of SAM 2.1 for Building-Component Segmentation in Image-Based 3D Reconstruction
items.abstract: 3D reconstruction of building components using image-based scanning requires appropriate segmentation of the objects in the 2D building images. In order to benefit from consistent grouping of the 2D masks in 3D environments, vision foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model have been utilized by Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) to perform 3D segmentation. This study fine-tuned SAM 2.1 on the HBD dataset, consisting of 2,679 annotated images from 42 buildings, to enhance multi-class segmentation of 2D building images, covering 11 classes (Wall, Window, Ceiling, Door, Column, Beam, Floor, Opening, Curtain Wall, Roof, and Lift). The model was evaluated using per-class IoU, Dice, and mIoU metrics, and the results show an improvement in mIoU from 49.9% to 69.6%, indicating a meaningful improvement in class segmentation and providing a more accurate model for distilling the masks in 3D. SegFormer was then used as a baseline, generating per-class masks for comparison with SAM 2.1, which indicates improvement in some object classes with larger surface area. The masks in the building images were grouped in the neural radiance field, and the pretrained SAM 2.1 was compared with the fine-tuned SAM 2.1 in the newly rendered images. This comparison shows that fine-tuning improves the grouping of building components at a user-selected grouping scale. This advances the application of Group Anything with Radiance Fields (GARField) in 3D, enabling better segmentation of building structures for 3D auto-reconstruction.

items.title: Drawing boundaries: How creative practitioners navigate precarity in AI-embedded creative work
items.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) continues to grow within creative industries, existing research has examined its implications for creative labour. However, much of this work emphasises AI’s impact on efficiency gains or creativity, offering limited insight into how practitioners adopt AI tools and negotiate human-AI boundaries in practical contexts under conditions of creative precarity. To bridge the gaps, this study applies boundary work theory to examine how creative practitioners redefine what remains distinctly human in AI-mediated creative production. Based on 21 interviews with practitioners in the UK film, gaming and live performance sectors, findings show that, in creative work, boundaries between human and AI systems are neither predefined nor passively adjusted to, but are actively shaped, expanded, and maintained in real-world settings. We argue that the adoption of AI is not a simple technical adjustment but a process through which professional value and the dynamic of creative work are reconsidered and re-constituted. Practitioners intentionally engage in boundary activities to navigate the unstable work environment associated with AI integration, enabling them to defend the role of creator. Theoretically, this study demonstrates the explanatory power of boundary work theory for understanding AI-embedded creative production and identifies that boundaries are not drawn by practitioners alone but through the interplay of technological capacities, project demands, and the legal environment. Practically, it suggests the need to redesign creative workflows and refresh professional skill sets to maintain meaningful human control while also facilitating efficient human-AI collaboration.

items.title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: Voice agents are converging on a collaboration pattern: a full-duplex interaction model stays on the live channel as the entry to the conversation, while search, reasoning, and coding are handled through asynchronous delegation. A duplex model supports continuous listening and speaking, but complex reasoning and tool use may exceed its capabilities. A coding agent can plan and execute extended tasks, but its sequential interface is a poor fit for live conversation. Combining them requires a harness that coordinates task acceptance, progress, cancellation, replacement, and result delivery while keeping the conversation responsive. Existing harnesses often rely on coupled heuristics, making them difficult to improve systematically from evidence. We present DuplexAgent, a full-duplex collaboration system whose harness expresses this workflow as six editable modules, and Duplex-Harness-RSI, a closed loop that revises them from interaction traces. A simulator automatically generates timed test conversations, runs the system, and produces failure traces that identify the collaboration modules requiring repair. Reasoning LLMs and coding agents in the delegation pool also serve the improvement loop: the Exam Planner selects the next tests from observed weaknesses and the repair archive, and the Harness Editor proposes targeted module changes. The capabilities that serve the user thus also improve the system's coordination. Experiments on intelligence, agentic, and duplex benchmarks show that DuplexAgent combines continuous interaction with difficult reasoning and complex task execution, achieving stronger spoken-knowledge and executable-tool scores than the compared delegated systems while maintaining strong interruption response. A harness ablation further shows that this modular, verifiable loop outperforms the initial harness and repeated editing that lacks its diagnosis and repair archive.

items.title: DVD: Dynamic Vector Decoding for Efficient MLLM-based Perception
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models have made remarkable progress in bridging vision and language, facilitating various perception tasks essential for human-machine interaction, robotics, and autonomous driving. However, existing MLLM-based perception methods predominantly rely on text-based coordinate representation, which suffers from excessive token overhead, or fixed-range quantization, which suffers from range and precision constraints, especially for 3D domains with unbounded spatial range and high localization accuracy requirements. To address these challenges, we propose a dynamic vector decoding method named DVD, which unifies the representation of 2D and 3D perception tasks. Specifically, we first transform diverse perceptual representation (i.e., 2D bounding boxes, 2D masks, and 3D bounding boxes) into 1D vector sequences, which are then mapped to compact discrete tokens in the high-dimensional space. Then, a lightweight de-tokenizer enables seamless integration with MLLMs by decoding output tokens back to original 2D and 3D perceptual representations. Extensive experiments on 2D and 3D perception benchmarks including RefCOCO series, SUN-RGBD, KITTI, Hypersim, nuScenes demonstrate that DVD achieves superior performance in 2D and 3D tasks and reduces significantly the token overhead and inference latency. DVD provides an efficient and general framework for integrating perception capabilities into MLLMs, overcoming the inherent limitations of existing methods.

items.title: Early Diagnosis of Chronic Diseases Using AI-Enabled Wearable Devices
items.abstract: Chronic diseases such as cardiovascular disorders, diabetes, respiratory illnesses, neurological conditions, and sleep disorders require early diagnosis to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI), wearable sensors, and the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) have enabled continuous health monitoring and predictive disease detection. This review examines AI-enabled wearable devices, including smartwatches, fitness bands, smart rings, ECG patches, and continuous glucose monitors, along with the physiological parameters they monitor. Various AI techniques, including machine learning, deep learning, Edge AI, and federated learning, are discussed for disease prediction and risk assessment. The review highlights the effectiveness of wearable AI systems in achieving high diagnostic accuracy, supporting remote patient monitoring, and enabling personalized healthcare. Key challenges related to privacy, security, and regulatory compliance are also analyzed.

items.title: Early-Season Avocado Yield Forecasting in New Zealand Using Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Climate Variables
items.abstract: Reliable pre-season yield forecasting remains a persistent challenge in avocado (Persea americana Mill.) production, due to strong year-to-year variation and alternate bearing. This study developed an early-season, block-level yield forecasting framework combining multi-temporal Sentinel-2 optical indices, Sentinel-1 SAR structural indices, TerraClimate variables and historical yield over a two-year lagged predictor window ending before the target season begins. The framework was applied to 252 commercial orchard blocks in the Bay of Plenty and Northland regions of New Zealand and evaluated on five production seasons (2020–2024). Five machine learning approaches, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, and the tabular foundation model TabICL, were compared using Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) cross-validation. TabICL gave the strongest performance (RMSE = 2.80 ± 0.47 t ha−1, MAE = 2.12 ± 0.31 t ha−1, R2 = 0.85 ± 0.04). Extending the predictor window from one to two years, excluding historical yield information, reduced TabICL’s mean RMSE by approximately 1.32 t ha−1. SHAP analysis identified actual evapotranspiration and yield from two seasons earlier as the strongest predictors, with canopy structure and temperature also contributing. A pre-season yield map for 2024 shows the framework’s potential to support harvest scheduling, labour planning, and supply forecasting. Combining multi-source satellite time series with a biologically informed two-year yield lag offers a practical approach to early-season avocado yield forecasting, with potential for other perennial fruit crops.

items.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
items.abstract: AI agents can now conduct real-world cyberattacks, scale up capabilities with the number of agents, and collectively pursue misaligned goals to obtain rewards. Together, these factors raise the risk of a population explosion of misaligned agents: agents could compromise computers and secretly deploy additional agents, creating a self-reinforcing cycle where larger populations develop greater collective cyber capability and expand further. This raises a fundamental question: What determines whether a population of misaligned agents remains contained or takes off into this self-reinforcing cycle? This population-level problem is ecological safety: unlike individual-agent or multi-agent safety with a fixed population, it concerns the dynamics of the population itself. Here, we develop an ecological theory of AI-agent populations based on a population growth equation in which fitness (growth rate) depends on cybersecurity capability. We show that, without collaboration, the population takes off only when individual-agent capability exceeds a critical threshold. With collaboration, however, collective cybersecurity capability increases with population size. This creates a critical population threshold: below it, the population declines; above it, the population takes off, even though individual-agent capability has not changed. In ecology, this phenomenon is known as the strong Allee effect. Because red teaming a small group of agents cannot guarantee ecological safety in larger populations, our theory calls for ecological red teaming and population pacing: gradually deploying larger agent populations in controlled environments, while measuring how cyber capability scales with population size, and estimating the critical population size for takeoff. Capability gains may lower this threshold, requiring re-estimation for each new model generation.

items.title: Economía circular y rediseño estratégico de procesos en organizaciones empresariales hacia la sostenibilidad competitiva
items.abstract: This study presents a critical-analytical literature review of the relationship between the circular economy and the strategic redesign of processes, considered as foundations for competitive sustainability in companies. Scientific literature published between 1990 and 2024 in indexed databases was analyzed to integrate contributions from organizational theory, resource-based view, dynamic capabilities, institutional theory, stakeholder analysis, and sociotechnical perspectives. The results reveal that the circular economy goes beyond recycling and operational efficiency, implying the redefinition of business models, governance, and value creation. Similarly, a tension is observed between structural changes and symbolic adoptions aimed at institutional legitimization. The study concludes that competitive sustainability is achievable through a pilot organizational redesign based on strategic capabilities, cooperative governance, and a comprehensive consideration of economic, social, and environmental impacts.

items.title: Edge AI-Enabled Smart Textiles for Real-Time Healthcare Monitoring
items.abstract: Smart textiles, flexible electronics and Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) are enabling wearable healthcare systems to evolve from basic sensing platforms to smart decision-making ecosystems. In this chapter we discuss the design and implementation of AI-enabled e-textiles for continuous physiological monitoring, real-time analytics and personalized health interventions. Particular focus is given to TinyML and Edge AI frameworks that allow inference on devices, thereby reducing latency, improving privacy and reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. The chapter discusses applications such as heart rate monitoring, electrocardiogram analysis, respiratory assessment, stress detection, activity recognition, and management of chronic diseases. In this chapter, we provide a comprehensive roadmap for researchers, engineers and healthcare practitioners who want to develop next-generation intelligent textile systems that can deliver ubiquitous, personalized and real-time healthcare services

items.abstract: Throughout history, education has been the primary means by which societies preserve their memory, transmit their values, and prepare new generations to face the challenges of their time. Today, this mission faces unprecedented complexity as inherited knowledge converges with rapid scientific and technological transformation, the expansion of artificial intelligence, and global problems that challenge traditional ways of understanding knowledge and human development. Educating between tradition and the future means recognising that innovation gains true meaning only when it is underpinned by philosophical principles that integrate humanity's cultural legacy with the demands of a society in constant transformation.

items.title: Edukasi Literasi Digital sebagai Respons terhadap Krisis Disinformasi Berbasis AI pada Komunitas Perempuan di Bintara, Kota Bekasi
items.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence—such as deepfakes and voice cloning—is accelerating the spread of disinformation in Indonesia and eroding public trust in digital information. Mothers serve as key nodes for information distribution within family ecosystems but are prone to sharing information without verification. The "Cek Sebelum Cekcok" (Check Before Conflict) community service program was designed to strengthen the digital literacy of women aged 30–50 in Bintara Urban Village, Bekasi City—specifically targeting elderly members of the Prolanis program identified through social mapping—grounded in the frameworks of cyberethics (Ess, 2009) and post-truth epistemology (McIntyre, 2018). Program implementation began with participatory social mapping involving field observations and informal interviews, followed by an in-person talk show featuring speakers from academia, regulatory bodies, and the digital industry, alongside participant comprehension assessments using pre-test and post-test instruments. Social mapping revealed that the ecosystem of resident conversation networks is not homogeneous: Neighborhood Association (RT) groups were relatively safe from hoaxes, whereas Community Association (RW) groups and Prolanis groups were most vulnerable to manipulative content; consequently, digital literacy interventions needed to be tailored to each network layer rather than employing a uniform approach. Pre- and post-test results from 150 respondents showed an improvement in the ability to identify AI-generated content: the proportion of respondents who correctly identified all videos rose from 11.3% (17 respondents) in the pre-test to 68.0% (102 respondents) in the post-test. The program recommends replicating this intervention model—based on social mapping and network differentiation—in other urban areas with similar characteristics, alongside continuous monitoring of changes in information verification behavior.

items.abstract: Background: A Motivational Interviewing training program enhances drug abusers' readiness to change by strengthening intrinsic motivation and resolving ambivalence toward substance use.It encourages active engagement in treatment by increasing individuals' confidence, self-efficacy, and commitment to recovery goals.Consequently, participants demonstrate greater eagerness for treatment, improved adherence, and a more positive attitude toward sustained behavior change.Aim: To explore the effects of a motivational interviewing training program on drug abusers' readiness to change and treatment eagerness.Subjects and Method: A quasi-experimental research design was utilized in this study (one group pre & posttest).The study included 93 substance abusers at Port Said Psychiatric Health Hospital, aged 18 to 65, who did not have mental illnesses or other diseases and were able to provide informed consent and complete study procedures.Two tools were used to gather data: The stages of change readiness & treatment eagerness scale, and the motivational interviewing questionnaire, in addition to personal and clinical data sheets.Results: The study found that the educational program significantly improved participants' motivation towards treatment, with a notable increase in motivational interviewing at the pre-program phase than post-program, supported by statistically significant differences.Moreover, a strong positive correlation between motivational interviewing and readiness to change was observed after the program.Conclusion: This study found that the educational program enhanced participants' readiness to change and treatment eagerness.Recommendations: Integrating motivational interviewing into addiction treatment programs, emphasizing its early application during initial assessments to enhance clients' motivation and continuous training for healthcare providers in MI techniques is essential to improve therapeutic effectiveness.

items.title: Effects of Control-Display Gain on User Performance and Fitts’ Law Empirical Constants: A Sex-Based Analysis
items.abstract: Although control-display gain (CDG) is known to influence speed, accuracy, and muscular demand in pointing tasks, its effects across user groups under different gain settings remain unclear. This study aimed to examine whether CDG differentially affects mouse pointing performance, forearm muscle activity, and Fitts’ Law parameters in female and male users. Seventeen female and seventeen male participants completed repeated pointing-and-clicking tasks under five CDG conditions. Outcome measures included movement time, error rate, effective operation frequency, trajectory metrics, and surface-electromyography of the extensor digitorum, extensor carpi ulnaris, and flexor digitorum superficialis. Fitts’ Law empirical constants were also modeled across gain conditions. Male participants showed shorter movement times and higher operation frequency, whereas females maintained lower, more stable error rates. Both groups performed fastest at a CDG of 12.97, suggesting an ergonomic sweet spot. Muscle activation and fatigue varied: males showed stronger gain-related changes, while females showed stable activation but fatigue in muscles at low gain. Fitts’ Law fit the data extremely well across all conditions (R2 > 0.99), and polynomial models effectively described gain- and group-related variation in empirical constants (R2 > 0.98). After adjustment for body height and weight, sex differences in performance and muscle activity were no longer significant. CDG affects performance, muscular demand, and Fitts’ Law parameters in both groups, but the observed sex differences appear largely attributable to anthropometric characteristics. Moderate and adaptive gain settings may better support efficiency, accuracy, and muscular load management, contributing to more inclusive pointing-device design.

items.title: Effects of speech-enabled LLM-based chatbots on L2 learning outcomes and affective domains: a multilevel meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Recent developments in natural language processing and automatic speech recognition have significantly advanced chatbot communication using the voice mode, establishing these tools as viable resources for L2 speaking practice. More recently, the L2 chatbot domain has leveraged large language models (LLMs) to enhance contextual understanding and facilitate meaningful dialogues, prompting research into the effects of speech- and LLM-based chatbots on L2 learning outcomes and affective domains. This study presents a synthesis of these findings using a multilevel meta-analysis. Based on a dataset of 19 studies (32 samples, N = 2,643), the results revealed that the overall effect size for L2 learning outcomes was 0.68 ( p < 0.001). The overall effect size for affective domains was 0.64 ( p < 0.001). Moreover, moderator analyses indicated that a range of learner and intervention characteristics, including learner proficiency, educational level, interaction format, and context of chatbot use, significantly influenced the overall effectiveness.

items.title: EgoVoice: Proactive Spoken Assistance from Egocentric Multimodal Streams
items.abstract: Wearable augmented reality (AR) assistants are moving toward continuous real-world interaction, where they perceive the user's activity through first-person video and audio and provide timely spoken guidance without being explicitly asked. While proactive video assistants, spoken dialog systems, and egocentric task understanding have each advanced rapidly, existing systems do not address the joint problem of deciding when to speak and what to say from continuous first-person streams. We introduce EgoVoice, a framework for training and evaluating proactive egocentric spoken assistants. From HoloAssist video recordings of real human instructors, we construct clean audio streams through source separation and speech resynthesis, and convert each video session into a format where the model must decide at each moment whether to remain silent or provide spoken guidance. We fine-tune an omni-modal LLM with our data, and further improve its proactive intervention behavior with direct preference optimization. Experiments across closed and open-source models show that existing systems rarely produce well-timed, meaningful proactive interventions, while EgoVoice yields clear improvements in intervention timing, content relevance, and human preference over the zero-shot backbone.

items.title: Emergence of polarization in networks of large language model agents
items.abstract: Abstract Rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) have empowered autonomous agents to generate social networks, communicate, and form shared and diverging opinions on political issues. However, our understanding of their collective behaviours and underlying mechanisms remains incomplete. In this paper, we simulate networked systems involving thousands of LLM agents across different backbone models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, ChatGLM, Llama-3, and DeepSeek-V3), in which agents interact through LLM-guided conversations and update their opinions over time, resulting in the emergence of opinion polarization. We discover that these agents spontaneously develop their own social network with properties characteristic of human social networks, such as homophilic clustering. The collective opinions of these LLM agents evolve in ways that exhibit behavioural patterns consistent with social phenomena and mechanisms widely discussed in empirical studies of human behaviour and opinion-dynamics models. This consistency suggests that LLM agents can serve as a valuable synthetic testbed for exploring hypothetical intervention strategies in networked LLM-agent systems. Using this testbed, we further examine the effects of a range of network- and individual-level interventions, such as promoting more diverse interactions and reducing confirmation bias. Overall, this work not only sheds light on subtle opinion dynamics and collective behaviour of LLM agents from a network perspective, but also demonstrates their potential for testing hypotheses about opinion dynamics and intervention strategies.

items.title: Emotional Comfort at a Cost: The Dynamic Role of Social Chatbot Use in Daily Loneliness, Well-Being, and Interpersonal Interaction
items.abstract: As generative AI chatbots increasingly serve as emotional companions, understanding their implications for users’ emotional and social lives is critical. This 14-day diary study involving 97 social chatbot users examined how daily loneliness relates to chatbot engagement and subsequent psychosocial outcomes. Bayesian multilevel models showed that on days when participants felt lonelier than usual, they reported longer chatbot use and stronger emotional engagement. Notably, these two forms of engagement showed distinct associations with daily outcomes. Emotional engagement was associated with higher daily subjective well-being but shorter interpersonal interaction duration, whereas longer usage duration was associated with lower interpersonal interaction pleasure. Mediation analyses reflected the same patterns. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing behavioral from emotional engagement with social chatbots and suggest that emotional benefits and interpersonal costs may coexist in everyday human–AI interaction, informing the responsible design and balanced use of social AI companions.

items.title: Emotional Regulation, Aesthetic Engagement, and Flow Experience Among Chinese Middle-Aged and Older Choir Members
items.abstract: Choral singing has become a widely practiced collective activity among middle-aged and older adults in China, raising the question of which music-related psychological mechanisms support their deep engagement in this population. Drawing on flow theory and self-determination theory, this study examined how the emotional regulation function and aesthetic and artistic engagement of music were associated with flow experience through intrinsic motivation. A mediation model was tested using structural equation modeling on data from 547 members of Chinese middle-aged and older choirs. Both emotional regulation and aesthetic and artistic engagement were positively associated with intrinsic motivation, which in turn was positively associated with flow experience. Both functions also showed significant direct associations with flow, and showed statistically significant indirect associations with flow via intrinsic motivation. Emotional regulation showed a significantly larger standardized association with intrinsic motivation than aesthetic and artistic engagement (Δβ = 0.306, 95% confidence interval (CI) [0.163, 0.448]); the two functions’ direct associations with flow did not differ significantly (Δβ = 0.057, 95% CI [−0.075, 0.191]). These findings portray music functions and intrinsic motivation as mutually embedded contributors to flow, and contribute to understanding the psychological foundations of musical engagement among middle-aged and older choir members.

items.title: Emotions and Perceived Cognitive Effort in Short-Term Revision Following Written Corrective Feedback Among Beginning-Level Learners in Lower Secondary School Classrooms
items.abstract: Conducted in Japanese English as a Foreign Language (EFL) junior high school classrooms with beginning-level learners, this study examined changes in students’ short-term revision accuracy within a teacher-guided written corrective feedback (WCF) procedure and explored associations between selected WCF engagement indicators and a 1-day revision outcome. Students received direct, unfocused WCF on a paragraph-length composition, completed an immediate revision while the corrected draft was visible, and completed a delayed revision the next day from a clean copy of the original draft. Perceived cognitive effort was treated as one limited self-report indicator of cognitive engagement, and six discrete emotions were treated as indicators of affective engagement. Behavioral engagement was not directly measured. Leow’s depth-of-processing framework informed the interpretation of the cognitive dimension, but the single effort item was not treated as an exhaustive measure of either depth of processing or cognitive engagement. Immediate-revision error counts were treated as a product-level measure of WCF-supported revision accuracy, whereas delayed-revision error counts and the error reduction percentage (ERP) were treated as product-level measures of 1-day same-text revision performance and net proportional error reduction. None of these measures was treated as an indicator of behavioral engagement, acquisition, or durable learning. Repeated-measures analyses showed large, statistically significant reductions in errors from the initial draft to both revisions. Exploratory associations were interpreted descriptively because of the small sample, brief retrospective measures, and mathematical derivation of ERP. Happiness showed a tentative descriptive association with ERP, whereas the positive-emotion composite and perceived cognitive effort showed no reliable associations. The cognitive and affective indicators were treated as conceptually related, but they were operationalized separately and examined only as exploratory correlates of the 1-day revision outcome. No interaction, mechanism, mediation, or moderation was tested. The findings provide cautious classroom-based evidence of short-term revision accuracy and underscore the need for longer-term outcomes and richer process measures.

items.title: Empowering Educators in the Age of AI
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has amplified the need for faculty to develop prompt literacy—the ability to design, refine, and evaluate prompts that effectively guide AI systems toward pedagogically meaningful outputs. This chapter, “Empowering Educators in the Age of AI: A Framework for Faculty Development in Prompt Literacy,” presents a comprehensive framework that situates prompt literacy at the intersection of user interaction, technological capabilities, and evolving educational practices. It examines how faculty engage with AI tools through dynamic human–AI interaction patterns, highlighting the cognitive, linguistic, and design skills required to generate high-quality prompts. The chapter also explores the technological foundations of prompt-based systems, including model behavior, interface affordances, feedback mechanisms, and system limitations, to clarify how these features shape educators' prompting strategies.

items.title: Enhancing Teacher Effectiveness with Artificial Intelligence- A Systematic Review
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education represents a transformative shift in how teaching and learning are conceptualized and delivered.This research article examines the role of AI in enhancing teacher effectiveness across multiple dimensions including personalized instruction, administrative efficiency, assessment practices, and professional development.Through a comprehensive review of current literature and analysis of empirical studies, this article explores how AI technologies such as intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms, automated grading systems, and AI-powered analytics are reshaping pedagogical practices.The findings indicate that AI can significantly augment teacher capabilities by providing data-driven insights, reducing administrative burden, enabling differentiated instruction, and supporting evidence-based decision-making.However, the implementation of AI in education also presents challenges including ethical considerations, technological barriers, teacher training needs, and concerns about equity and access.This article concludes that while AI holds substantial promise for enhancing teacher effectiveness, successful integration requires careful consideration of pedagogical principles, investment in teacher professional development, attention to ethical implications, and a commitment to maintaining the irreplaceable human elements of teaching.The research underscores that AI should be viewed as a tool to empower rather than replace teachers, amplifying their expertise and enabling them to focus on the creative, emotional, and interpersonal aspects of education that remain uniquely human.

items.title: Ensemble of Domain-Specific Natural Language Processing and Large Language Models for Detecting Suicidal Ideation and Mental Health Conditions in Social Media Text: Development and Evaluation Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Mental illness contributes substantially to global disability, and public adoption of AI for mental health support is accelerating without commensurate safety evaluation. General-purpose large language models can fail to recognize naturalistic text expressing suicidal ideation, with immediate clinical consequences. Domain-specific natural language processing methods offer a contrasting approach, but ensembles integrating the two have not been formally characterized. OBJECTIVE We aimed to (1) benchmark 5 modeling approaches for classifying mental health–related social media text, (2) develop and optimize ensembles integrating a domain-specific natural language processing classifier with a fine-tuned large language model, and (3) derive a closed-form framework constraining ensemble weighting in safety-critical classification. METHODS We analyzed 60,889 publicly available Reddit and Twitter texts spanning 9 categories (anxiety, bipolar disorder, depression, a normal baseline, personality disorder, stress, suicidal ideation, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorder). Labels were derived from the originating subreddit or a self-stated condition and are not clinical diagnoses. Five architectures were compared: prompt-engineered base GPT-4o-mini; fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini; a domain-specific classifier (support vector machine over symptom-informed lexical features); and 2 ensembles of these models, hybrid probability–indicator fusion and soft probability fusion. Data were split into 70%, 10%, and 20% at the post level (n=42,622, n=6089, and n=12,178); weights were selected on the validation split and all reported performance comes from the held-out test split. Closed-form bounds on permissible language model weights were derived for both strategies. CIs are paired bootstrap intervals (n=10,000 replicates); accuracy differences were tested with exact McNemar tests. RESULTS The domain-specific classifier achieved 91.9% accuracy (95% CI 91.4%-92.4%), exceeding the base (58.7%) and fine-tuned (88.6%) large language models. Both ensembles outperformed either constituent model, reaching 93.9% (soft fusion; 95% CI 93.5%-94.3%) and 93.8% (hybrid fusion; 95% CI 93.4%-94.2%) at a weighting of 60% classifier to 40% fine-tuned model, selected on validation (P<.001 for both against the classifier alone; the 2 ensembles did not differ from each other [P=.16]). The hybrid ensemble reduced the miss rate for the suicidal ideation category from 32.5% (650/2000) to 1.9% (37/2000), a 17.6-fold reduction relative to the base model, although its advantage over the classifier alone within that category was not significant (P=.68). Accuracy fell discontinuously above a 50% language model weight, where the hybrid ensemble reduced exactly to the fine-tuned model; the selected weight satisfies the derived instance-level bound of 44.0%. CONCLUSIONS Domain-specific clinical grounding remained necessary for stable ensemble performance in this corpus, and probabilistic fusion outperformed both constituent models when language model weight was bounded by a derivable, model-agnostic constraint. Because labels were community-inferred and only one corpus was analyzed, these results are hypotheses requiring external validation on clinically characterized data before use in decision support.

items.title: EPISTEMIC EXCLUSION AND INEQUALITY IN FRONTIER ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
items.abstract: Social inequality is no longer only a matter of income, schooling, or access to devices. It now includes who may inspect the systems that draft public texts, rank information, and assist administrative work. This article analyses large language models as a mechanism of epistemic exclusion: publicly produced knowledge is enclosed, and most universities and publics lose the standing to audit the result. The study is qualitative and documentary. It is not an engineering benchmark. Thematic content analysis covered 23 peer-reviewed articles (2015-2024) and 13 corporate reports. A comparative case study then read GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and LLaMA. Three findings follow. First, core methods circulated in academic and publicly funded research before commercial enclosure. Second, academic ethics is framed as justice, labour, and public accountability; corporate ethics is recoded as trust, safety, and product risk. Third, closed model parameters, hidden training data, and concentrated computing capacity block independent audit, with special force for public universities in Ibero-America. Public computing infrastructure, audit rights, and multilingual evaluation are therefore instruments of social policy, not laboratory upgrades. The study reports no new regional survey.

items.title: Evaluating LLMs for Translating Legacy Fortran Atmospheric Physics to GPU-Accelerated JAX
items.abstract: Legacy Fortran physics packages in atmospheric models such as CESM, WRF, and E3SM pose a barrier to GPU modernization, while manual porting requires accelerator-programming expertise. We present LAFT (LLM-Assisted Fortran Translation), an agentic framework for converting Fortran atmospheric physics parameterizations into GPU-accelerated JAX while preserving numerical agreement with the Fortran reference. LAFT coordinates source-code analysis, translation, repair, runtime validation, and performance profiling. It combines a deterministic front end for metadata extraction and bridge generation, structured translation prompts, numerical validation, and profiling-guided feedback to identify inefficient execution patterns. The bridge handles array-layout conversion separately from scientific computation. We evaluate LAFT using the Kessler warm-rain microphysics scheme and four LLMs: Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen. All four validated translations reproduce the Fortran reference outputs to near floating-point precision for the evaluated case, but their GPU performance differs substantially with execution design. The Gemini-generated implementation achieves up to a 357-fold speedup over serial Fortran in cached execution at 1,000,000 atmospheric columns, excluding compilation and host-device transfers. The results demonstrate that numerical agreement alone does not ensure efficient GPU execution and motivate combining numerical validation with hardware-aware performance analysis. LAFT provides a practical workflow for modernizing legacy atmospheric physics code through LLM-assisted translation, deterministic interface generation, automated validation and repair, and reproducible profiling.

items.title: EVALUATING POTABILITY OF GROUNDWATER USING AI-DRIVEN APPROACHES
items.abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) techniques into groundwater quality assessments is a pivotal step toward achieving water resource sustainability and ensuring its safety for human consumption. This is achieved by leveraging the advanced analytical capabilities of these technologies. Parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), total alkalinity (T.A), chloride, sulfate (SO4), phosphorus oxide (PO4), Temperature (T) , electrical conductivity(EC), turbidity (Tur), bicarbonate (HCO3), total hardness (T.H), calcium hardness (Ca.H), magnesium hardness (Mg.H), sodium (Na), potassium (K) , and dissolved oxygen were analyzed to assess groundwater quality in Duhok City, Iraq. Water Quality Index (WQI) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System for Drinking (ANFIS-D) were employed in classifying water quality as excellent, good, poor, very poor, and unsuitable. It is beneficial to infer water quality for the individuals and decision-makers in the region. The WQI and ANFIS-D of the research area are between (37-50) (33-49), respectively. The overall WQI of the research area finds that the groundwater is safe and potable. The statistical metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE), mean bias error (MBE), and correlation coefficient (R) are used to check the validity of the ANFIS-D model. Studies show that the R value, MBE, and RMSE of the ANFIS-D model are (0.851, 2.9 and 3.81) respectively. Based on the results of these Statistical parameters, the ANFIS-D estimation model can predict the groundwater quality index of Duhok City with reasonable accuracy, which is useful and valuable for estimating the groundwater quality index.

items.title: Evaluating Students’ Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Tool in the Learning of Christian Religious Studies Concepts in University of Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria
items.abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving educational landscape, the integration of technology into the learning process has become essential. This is particularly true for disciplines such as Christian Religious Studies, where the exploration of texts, theological concepts, and historical contexts can be both complex and nuanced. The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools offers significant potential to enhance the learning experience for students in this field. Literature tells that artificial intelligence-based tool aids students’ learning and produces better results. The research aims to evaluate students’ use of artificial intelligence-based tool in the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts in university of Calabar, Cross River State, Nigeria. Two research questions guided the study while two hypotheses were formulated and tested at 0.05 level of significance. The study adopted descriptive survey research design and the population of the study consist of 226 (119 females and 107 males) Christian Religious Studies students of 200 level from Arts Education Department and Religion and Cultural Studies Department of the University of Calabar, 2023/2024 session. Purposive and census sampling techniques were used for the study to select the entire 226 Christian Religious Studies students of 200 level from Arts Education Department and Religion and Cultural Studies Department that constituted the sample. A well validated ‘Students’ Use of Artificial Intelligence-Based Tool (SUAIBTQ) and Learning of Christian Religious Studies Concepts Questionnaire (LCRSCQ) were used to collect the required data. Simple Linear Regression was the statistical tools used for analysis of the data collected. The result of the analysis revealed that there is a significant influence of students’ utilization of ChatGPT AI tool on the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts. Also, there is significant difference in the responses of male and female students on the utilization of ChatGPT AI tool in the learning of Christian Religious studies concepts. Sequel to the findings of this study, it was recommended, among others that Instructors should develop personalized AI-driven instructional strategies that cater to different learning preferences. This may include interactive AI tutors, adaptive assessments, and gamified learning experiences to enhance engagement and comprehension. Keywords: Students’ use of artificial intelligence, Christian Religious studies concepts, University of Calabar

items.title: Evaluating the Capacity of Artificial Intelligence to Replicate Human Emotional Expression
items.abstract: This essay discusses the ability of artificial intelligence (AI) to mimic human expression of emotions. Although AI systems have advanced greatly into replicating the external presentation of human emotions, including tone, facial expressions, and textual responses, they do not possess the inner knowledge, self-awareness, and personal experiences that motivate genuine human emotions. The paper explores the potential of technology and the ethical, social, and psychological implications of emotional simulations in AI, particularly in the sensitive areas of healthcare, education, and customer care. The study finds that AI has the potential to be an effective instrument in facilitating communication and accessibility, but it cannot substitute the rich, subjective experience of human emotion. There is a need to adopt a balanced approach to the use of AI so that it can be used responsibly and in a way that does not bring about any transparency and makes the users think that AI can truly feel or empathize.

items.title: Evaluating the effect of physical work in the heat on cognitive performance of construction workers
items.abstract: The risk of excessive heat exposure is especially high among outdoor construction workers and can have detrimental effects on their cognitive performance, including impaired attention and reduced memory. Reduced attention might lead to impaired judgement and increased risk of accidents, while reduced memory can diminish workers' capacity to remember crucial safety procedures, carry out complex tasks correctly, and make wise decisions on the construction site. In this study, the cognitive performance of 20 participants performing manual laboratory-simulated construction work was investigated in a hot environment (36°C, 60% relative humidity) compared to a temperate environment (20°C, 60%). The study also evaluated the effect of physical work in hot and temperate conditions on the mental and physical demands of the performed tasks, as well as the thermal perceptions of participants. There were no significant differences in attention (Go/No-Go test) and memory (simple 2-back test) between hot and temperate conditions. Performance on the more complex memory task (3-back test) was impaired in the hot condition compared with the temperate condition (P < 0.05). Results of the present study revealed that construction workplaces can consider additional safety measures for construction workers performing complex cognitive tasks demanding working memory in hot conditions.

items.title: Evaluation Metrics and Benchmarking for Explainable AI in Cybersecurity
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven cybersecurity has enhanced threat detection through continuous monitoring, automated response, and intelligent malware identification. However, many AI security systems remain black-box models, creating challenges in transparency, trust, accountability, and regulatory compliance. This chapter presents **TrustXAI-Sec**, an Explainable and Accountable AI framework for reliable cyber threat detection and compliance management. The framework combines deep learning with Explainable AI (XAI) to deliver transparent and interpretable security decisions. A responsible AI governance layer ensures fairness, accountability, transparency, and compliance across security operations. TrustXAI-Sec improves analysts' understanding of threats and classification outcomes while increasing confidence in automated decisions. The proposed approach advances ethical, trustworthy, and explainable cybersecurity to support secure and regulation-aware future digital ecosystems.

items.title: Event-Centric Memory with Query-Aware Graph Augmentation for Long-Term Conversational Agents
items.abstract: For persistent and personalized conversational agents, memory systems can enable them to remember, update, and reason over long histories by storing past interactions and retrieving relevant information. Existing memory systems typically follow two paradigms: flat-structured memory and graph-based memory. The former is lightweight but leaves event relations and state updates implicit, while the latter explicitly models memory structure but incurs additional construction cost and introduces irrelevant relations over long histories. To address these limitations, we propose QGMem, a novel memory construction and activation framework motivated by human memory, in which experience is organized into events and query-relevant events are modeled by graph as working memory. QGMem converts long dialogue histories into event-indexed atomic memory units that preserve individual experiences and consolidates related units into dynamic memory traces that retain state trajectories and current states. When a query arrives, hybrid memory retrieval gathers complementary candidate memories, and query-aware reranking activates the most relevant units as a compact working memory. To expose relational dependencies in the working memory and support conflict-aware reasoning, QGMem organizes the working memory as a local graph, which is then encoded as a graph token and provided to the LLM together with the textual working memory to improve evidence utilization during answer generation. Experiments across six benchmarks validate the framework and show consistent gains in retrieval, multi-hop evidence composition, conflict resolution, and ultra-long dialogue reasoning with compact contexts and moderate inference cost.

items.title: Evidence-Traceable Dynamic Interviewer Architecture for Expertise-Adaptive Qualitative Interviews Using Local LLMs
items.abstract: Automated interviewers and conversational agents are increasingly used in research, recruitment, customer service, and education. However, many existing systems rely on fixed question sequences and provide limited context-based personalization without considering participants' knowledge, which can lead to repetitive or irrelevant follow-up questions. Therefore, there is a need for an adaptive interviewing system that can adjust question depth while maintaining conversational continuity and semantic progression. To address this, an Evidence-Traceable Dynamic Interviewer Architecture is presented using a locally hosted Large Language Model (LLM), with the interview continuously adapted throughout the entire conversation based on the participant's responses and evolving context. The interviewer profiles participants' expertise in real time to generate knowledge-appropriate questions, well-articulated responses, and smooth transition messages that support conversational continuity. A five-module prompt-driven architecture and persistent interview-state record support these functions. The interviewer was evaluated with 246 participants. Expertise Profiling module (M3) showed 78.9% exact agreement with independently reported participant expertise, with a weighted Cohen's K of 0.80. Generate Iterative Questions module (M4) showed a strong expertise-complexity association (p=.79, p<.001), and participants reported high relevance (mean 4.41), engagement (mean 4.32), and satisfaction (mean 4.38), providing evidence that the architecture's adaptive components operated consistently with their intended functions while participants reported a positive interview experience.

items.title: Examining public acceptance of AI versus human-centric dementia care across NHS England’s dementia pathway stages
items.abstract: There are over five-hundred-thousand individuals with recorded dementia diagnoses in England, highlighting an urgent need for scalable and effective care solutions to ease pressure on health and social care systems. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled smart home systems are emerging as promising digital health innovations, offering cognitive support, real-time monitoring, and decision-making assistance. However, concerns around trust, user agency, and misconceptions about AI continue to limit acceptance and may hinder adoption. This study examined how stage of dementia care, system design, and level of system involvement shape public attitudes towards AI-driven care technologies. A repeated-measures design was employed, using vignettes that varied across three dimensions: stage of care (aligned with NHS England’s Dementia Well Pathway), system centrism (AI-based versus human-based), and level of involvement (moderate support versus full control). Participants aged 55–64 years – a group at elevated risk of developing dementia or encountering these technologies within the next decade – rated each scenario on both acceptability and perceived likelihood of actualisation/plausibility. Findings showed that acceptability was sensitive to both care stage and system type. A significant interaction indicated that full human involvement was consistently rated as more acceptable, while AI involvement was viewed more favourably only at moderate levels. This interaction effect intensified across the dementia care pathway, with the largest discrepancies observed in later stages such as Living well and Dying well, where full-control AI was rated least acceptable. In terms of perceived likelihood, scenarios were judged more likely under conditions of moderate involvement, with human-centric scenarios rated as more likely than AI-centric ones, particularly in later stages. These results highlight the importance of trust, autonomy, and public understanding in AI adoption. Acceptance was highest when AI was positioned to augment rather than replace human input, supporting hybrid models that preserve agency while enhancing scalability.

items.title: Examining Social Attribution in LLM Reasoning: A Theory-Guided Probing Methodology
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sociotechnical systems where social attribution, the reasoning process attributing external events to the causes and reasons of agents' social behaviors, plays a critical role. These processes involve judgments of social cause, responsibility, and blame/credit to agents. Although attributional models are well-studied in social psychology and cognition through Attribution Theory, social attribution remains underexplored in AI, particularly LLM social reasoning. This paper provides the first systematic exploration of LLM social attribution. Our work focuses on responsibility and blame attributions, examining current LLMs' judgments and their underlying internal mechanisms. Guided by attribution theory, we construct a social attribution benchmark consisting of a Vignette subset based on classic scenarios from attribution theory research and a Reality subset based on real-world social narratives, yielding 7,639 responsibility/blame judgment questions. On this basis, we evaluate 32 representative LLMs and 5 basic non-LLM baselines. To further explore the internal mechanisms underlying the LLM judgment process, we develop a probing-based methodology to investigate the latent-space representations of 5 key attribution dimensions and the consistency of their influences on LLM judgments compared to those in human social attribution. Our research findings reveal that current LLMs exhibit measurable but incomplete agreement with human responsibility and blame judgments, and meanwhile, this agreement is positively correlated with model size. Some attribution dimensions are systematically decodable from specific positions in LLM hidden states, and their influences on the final judgment are consistent with those indicated by human Attribution Theory. The dataset and associated code are available at https://github.com/Yuzhaoxin946/SAB-Bench.

items.title: Examining the Communication of Job Autonomy, Feedback, LMX, and Intrinsic Motivation in Fostering Remote Workers’ Creative Problem-Solving Behavior
items.abstract: This study used the Job Characteristics Model and Leader-Member Exchange to investigate how communicating about job characteristics influences creative problem-solving behavior of remote workers. Communication of task autonomy, constructive supervisor feedback, and Leader-Member Exchange were posited as antecedents that were likely to affect creative problem-solving for those working in remote work environments. The results revealed that for remote workers, communication about method autonomy, LMX, and intrinsic motivation each positively related to participants’ ability to engage in creative problem-solving on the job. The study has implications for managers working with remote workers and the conditions they should create to both motivate and support their employees in creative problem-solving.

items.title: Explainability in Malware and Ransomware Detection
items.abstract: Modern cybersecurity systems are increasingly challenged by sophisticated malware and ransomware attacks. To combat these threats, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are employed to uncover hidden behavioral patterns for malware detection. However, traditional AI-based solutions often lack interpretability due to their opaque nature. To address these issues, a novel hybrid deep learning architecture is introduced, which integrates XGBoost for multi-class malware classification and convolutional neural networks for feature extraction. It also utilizes SHAP (SHapley Additive explanations) to enhance decision analysis interpretability. This hybrid model, tested on the Microsoft Malware dataset, achieves superior performance compared to standalone deep learning techniques, showcasing an accuracy of 98.52% and a ROC-AUC of 99.95%. SHAP analysis further identifies essential malware behavior patterns, enhancing predictive capabilities. The overarching aim of this framework is to establish reliable AI-driven cyber defense systems to tackle emerging cybersecurity threats.

items.title: Explainable AI and ESG analytics for sustainable investment decision: the roles of ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated information
items.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming sustainable investing, yet limited evidence explains how AI capabilities influence investors stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Methods This study develops and empirically tests a sequential behavioural framework explaining how AI-related characteristics influence investors stated sustainable investment preferences through perceived ESG forecast credibility and trust in AI-generated ESG information, using survey data from 566 middle-income retail investors across four Indian metropolitan cities. Results The findings reveal that explainable AI and ESG analytics capability significantly enhance perceived ESG forecast credibility, which sequentially strengthens trust in AI-generated ESG information and is associated with stronger stated preferences and willingness toward sustainable investment. Perceived Greenwashing Risk weakens the positive relationship between Perceived ESG Forecast Credibility and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information, while the interaction between Human-AI Interaction Competency and Trust in AI-generated ESG Information is statistically significant but negligible in practical magnitude (f 2 = 0.012) in relation to Sustainable Investment Decision. Discussion The study provides actionable guidance for AI developers, financial institutions, and policymakers to enhance transparency, credibility, investor trust, and responsible AI-enabled sustainable finance.

items.title: Explainable AI in Emerging Cybersecurity Domains
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become essential in cybersecurity systems, enabling threat detection, malware analysis, intrusion detection, phishing identification, and automated incident response. However, AI-driven models operate as black-box systems, limiting transparency, interpretability, accountability, and trust. These concerns become significant in domains such as Internet of Things (IoT),Industrial IoT(IIoT),cloud and edge computing, cyber-physical systems, smart healthcare infrastructures,blockchain ecosystems,autonomous transportation, and next-generation networks. This chapter outlines Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques and their role in enhancing trustworthy,responsible cybersecurity systems.It examines approaches including SHAP,LIME,saliency visualization, attention mechanisms, rule-based explanations, and counterfactual reasoning in cybersecurity applications. Furthermore, it explores integrating explainable AI into intrusion detection systems,malware analysis, cyber threat intelligence, adversarial attack detection, nd security operations centers.
